nodes.title: Transparent frameless window shows white corners on focus loss (DWM inactive frame)
nodes.body:
## Problem

On Windows 11, a transparent frameless window (`frame: false` + `transparent: true` + `roundedCorners: false`) with CSS `clipPath: inset(0 round 16px)` for rounded corners renders white rectangular blocks outside the CSS rounded corners when the window loses focus. This appears to be DWM rendering an inactive frame decoration over the transparent areas.

## Environment

- Electron 35.0.0
- Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
- Node.js 24.14.1

## BrowserWindow options

```js
new BrowserWindow({
  frame: false,
  titleBarStyle: 'hidden',
  transparent: true,
  thickFrame: false,
  roundedCorners: false,
  backgroundMaterial: 'none',
  backgroundColor: '#00000000',
})
```

## What I've tried

1. **`setShape()`** — Prevents the white corners, but the rectangle-approximated rounded shape has visible aliasing/jagged edges. No `{ rect, radius }` format supported (TypeError).

2. **`DwmSetWindowAttribute` with `DWMWA_NCRENDERING_POLICY = DWMNCRP_DISABLED`** — Called via PowerShell P/Invoke before window shows. No HRESULT error, but white corners still appear on focus loss.

3. **`DWMWA_BORDER_COLOR = DWMWA_COLOR_NONE`** — Same result, no effect.

4. **`DwmExtendFrameIntoClientArea` with `MARGINS = {-1,-1,-1,-1}`** — Same result, no effect.

5. **`show: false` + apply DWM fixes before `window.show()`** — Attempted to set DWM attributes before DWM's first render. Still no effect.

6. **Re-applying DWM fixes on `focus`/`blur` events** — No effect.

## Expected behavior

The white inactive-frame corners should not appear when the window loses focus, allowing CSS `clipPath`/`border-radius` to provide smooth rounded corners without `setShape()`.

## Question

Is there a way to prevent DWM from rendering the inactive frame on transparent frameless windows? Or is `setShape()` the only option, and if so, is there a plan to support rounded corner shapes (e.g. `{ rect, radius }` format)?

nodes.title: Bug: Windows notifications stopped working since v42.0.0-beta.4 (Regression from PR #50895)
nodes.body:

### Electron Version

v42.0.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 10 Pro 22H2

### What arch are you using?

ia32

### Last Known Working Electron version

v41.6.1 / v42.0.0-beta.3

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Calling `new Notification(options).show()` should trigger and display native Windows toast notifications normally, as it did in Electron v41.

### Actual Behavior

Windows notifications completely fail to render or appear in the Action Center since `v42.0.0-beta.4`. The API fails silently without throwing any errors or crashing the application process. This behaviour directly coincides with the implementation of PR #50895 ("feat: add id, groupId, and groupTitle support for Windows notifications"), which introduced new Windows-specific notification parameters.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

- Architecture details: The application is being cross-compiled as a 32-bit binary (ia32) and executed on a 64-bit Windows OS (x64). 
- Regression tracking: The issue is fully reproducible starting from v42.0.0-beta.4. Downgrading the binary to any v41 release restores the expected notification behaviour instantly, confirming a regression introduced by changes in PR #50895.

26.5

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.5.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Creating a module Worker in preload should not block `webContents.send()` delivery to the renderer when launched from VS Code with type: `chrome` and  `--remote-debugging-port=9222`. Opening DevTools should not change IPC delivery

### Actual Behavior

Preload creates `new Worker('./worker.js', { type: 'module' })` on `window.load`. 1s after `did-finish-load`, `main` calls `webContents.send('show-grid', ...)`. The renderer's handler never fires — spinner stays, grid never appears. Opening DevTools immediately flushes the queued handler; the logged delay equals the time spent stuck. Removing the Worker, or launching via `npm start` or `npm run start-cdp`, avoids the stall.

This worked in Electron 41.5.0.

[repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27787261/repro.zip)

  - `locales/` folder with multiple language packs

```
dist/
├── electron.exe                    (~216 MB) ✓ REQUIRED
├── version                        (~5 bytes) ✓ REQUIRED
├── resources/
│   ├── app/
│   ├── crashpad_handler.exe
│   ├── icudtl.dat
│   └── ...
├── locales/
│   ├── am.pak
│   ├── ar.pak
│   ├── bg.pak
│   ├── el.pak
│   ├── ... (75 files total)
│   └── zh-TW.pak
├── LICENSES.chromium.html
└── ...

#### Actual Behavior

**Actual `dist/` directory contents:**
```
dist/
└── locales/
    └── el.pak    (1.16 MB) ← Only this single file exists!
```

nodes.title: Allow overriding MPRIS service name
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, [Chromium hardcodes MPRIS service name](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:components/system_media_controls/linux/system_media_controls_linux.cc;l=141;drc=c83b80f441edc1c50de8d3977fa3feeb0ae96bc3) as `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.chromium.instance<pid here>`, thus preventing the app from accessing MPRIS bus within Flatpak sandbox environment ([Flatpak only allows](https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/sandbox-permissions.html#d-bus-access) `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.$FLATPAK_ID` service name).

As a result, `MediaSession` will not be able to work properly within Flatpak environment.

### Proposed Solution

Allow the app to set its custom MPRIS suffix, e.g. `app.setMPRISServiceName("abc")` sets service name to `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.abc`.

### Alternatives Considered

None as of now

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Crash (SIGSEGV) on right-click in -webkit-app-region: drag on macOS 26
nodes.body:
## Description Right-clicking on an element with `-webkit-app-region: drag` in a `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` window causes a SIGSEGV crash (null pointer dereference at address 0x0) on macOS 26 (Tahoe, build 25C56). The crash occurs inside `[ElectronNSWindow sendEvent:]` → `[super sendEvent:]` when processing `NSEventTypeRightMouseDown`. The `sendEvent` override temporarily disables draggable regions via `WebContents::SetDisableDraggableRegions(true)`, which makes `draggable_region()` return `nullptr`. Something in Chromium's event routing then dereferences this null pointer. ## Versions - Tested on Electron 42.0.1 (Chromium 148) and 43.0.0-alpha.1 (Chromium 149) — both crash - Electron 41.3.0 does NOT crash - macOS 26.2 (25C56), Apple Silicon (Mac16,6) ## Minimal Reproduction ```js // main.js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron'); app.whenReady().then(() => { const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600, titleBarStyle: 'hidden', webPreferences: { nodeIntegration: false, contextIsolation: true } }); win.loadURL('data:text/html,
RIGHT CLICK HERE TO CRASH
Content area
'); }); ``` ```json // package.json {"name":"crash-test","version":"1.0.0","main":"main.js"} ``` Steps: 1. Run `npx electron .` 2. Right-click on the gray "RIGHT CLICK HERE TO CRASH" bar 3. App crashes with SIGSEGV ## Crash Report (key frames) ``` Exception Type: EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000 Thread 0 Crashed:: CrBrowserMain 0 Electron Framework 0x114526b88 ... 7 AppKit 0x190e3c860 -[NSApplication(NSEventRouting) sendEvent:] + 1276 8 Electron Framework 0x10e92a9bc ``` ## Analysis The crash path is in `shell/browser/ui/cocoa/electron_ns_window.mm` line 224-243. The `sendEvent:` override calls `SetDisableDraggableRegions(true)` before `[super sendEvent:event]`. This makes `WebContents::draggable_region()` return `nullptr` (line 2191 of `electron_api_web_contents.cc`). On macOS 26, the Chromium event handler inside `[super sendEvent:]` appears to dereference this null pointer. This did NOT crash on macOS 15 or Electron 41. ## Expected Behavior Right-clicking on a drag region should show a context menu (or do nothing), not crash.

nodes.title: ci: run tests at different DPI scales on Windows
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Some new regressions and longstanding issues on Windows are hard to catch because the tests all pass at 100% display scale: #51572, #10862, #51385, #47296, etc.

### Proposed Solution

In order from easiest to most involved:

- Run some bounds/constraints/resizing tests at non-100% DPIs, e.g. a 200% test for integer scaling, and a 175% test for hard-mode.
- Run tests with multiple monitors at different scale factors.
- Run tests across DPI scale changes in the middle of the test.

### Alternatives Considered

We should also consider patching Chromium or contributing more upstream so it handles DPI more transparently/precisely on Windows, which would simplify API design and maintenance in Electron which is currently full of edge cases.

### Additional Information

_No response_

Set the display scale to 175% in Windows and  create an 800x600 window with `frame: false`. The dimensions of the window, content, and viewport should all be 800x600:

```
Window: { x: 697, y: 293, width: 800, height: 600 }
Content: { x: 697, y: 293, width: 800, height: 600 }
[9020:0509/104305.113:INFO:CONSOLE:21] "Viewport: 800 x 600", source:  (21)
```

### Actual Behavior

The dimensions are sometimes off by 1-3 px.
```
Window { x: 705, y: 293, width: 801, height: 601 }
Content { x: 704, y: 293, width: 803, height: 602 }
[7776:0509/104549.114:INFO:CONSOLE:24] "Viewport width: 803, height: 602", source:  (24)
```

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/599154630e98fb1773ba6731feaee5cd

### Additional Information

I can reproduce this issue to some extent in versions of Electron as far back as 38.0, but my recent work on resize insets (https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50706) has made the drift more obvious (from 1px to 3px depending on scale and the values).

I believe it is caused by inconsistent rounding in Chromium when bounds are provided in DIP pixels.

nodes.title: setDisplayMediaRequestHandler useSystemPicker crashes after custom handler capture on macOS
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.0.1, 39.8.10

### What operating system are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.4 / Darwin 25.4.0

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A

### Expected Behavior

An app should be able to use a custom `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler(..., { useSystemPicker: false })` flow for one `getDisplayMedia()` request, stop all returned tracks, and then later switch to `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler(..., { useSystemPicker: true })` for a subsequent `getDisplayMedia()` request without hanging or crashing.

### Actual Behavior

After a custom handler capture completes and all tracks are stopped, switching the same Electron session back to `useSystemPicker: true` can crash the process when a source is selected in the macOS system picker.

The crash is native and cannot be caught in JavaScript:

```text
*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception 'NSGenericException', reason: '*** Collection <__NSArrayM: ...> was mutated while being enumerated.'
*** First throw call stack:
(
  0   CoreFoundation                      __exceptionPreprocess
  1   libobjc.A.dylib                     objc_exception_throw
  2   CoreFoundation                      -[__NSSingleObjectEnumerator description]
  3   ScreenCaptureKit                    -[SCContentSharingPicker contentPickerDidSelectFilter:forStream:]
  4   ReplayKit                           -[RPScreenRecorder contentPickerDidSelectFilter:forStream:]
  5   ReplayKit                           -[RPDaemonProxy contentPickerDidSelectFilter:forStream:]
  ...
)
Electron exited with signal SIGTRAP
```

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the gist below.
2. Run `npm install`.
3. Run `npm start`.
4. Click `1. Custom picker capture`.
5. In the in-app custom source list, select a window.
6. Wait for the local preview to start.
7. Click `2. Stop tracks`.
8. Click `3. System picker capture`.
9. In the macOS system picker, select the same window.
10. The app crashes with the native ScreenCaptureKit stack above.

Control behavior: if `3. System picker capture` is used first after app start, the system picker works.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/3777de2ac0a21630326fda9039e9762e

### Additional Information

The minimal repro does not use any app-specific code or WebRTC publishing. It only uses:

- `desktopCapturer.getSources()` for the custom source list
- `session.defaultSession.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler(handler, { useSystemPicker: false })`
- `navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia()`
- `MediaStreamTrack.stop()`
- then `session.defaultSession.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler(handler, { useSystemPicker: true })`
- then `navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia()` again

I also tested stronger cleanup before switching back to system picker, including clearing references and stopping tracks. The crash still occurs, suggesting the issue is in the same-session transition from a custom handler capture to the macOS system picker.

### Electron Version

Electron Version: 35.7.5 (also tested 31.7.7, 33.4.11)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.3

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

35.7.5

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When typing Chinese (using IME input methods such as Pinyin) inside a textarea in an Electron application on macOS, the IME candidate window should:

* Display correctly under or near the text cursor
* Show full candidate list (not only pre-edit text / pinyin)
* Follow the caret position accurately during typing
* Behave consistently with native applications and Chrome browser

### Actual Behavior

On macOS (26.3 / Tahoe), when using Electron (tested with Electron 31 - Electron 35) with a minimal reproduction project:

* IME input still works (pinyin composition is visible)
* However, the candidate window does not display correctly
    * In some cases, only the pinyin/pre-edit text is shown
    * Candidate list is missing or not rendered
    * Candidate window may appear empty or not attached to the input field
* The issue persists even in a minimal Electron application with a single <textarea> and no custom CSS or layout
* The same input method works correctly in Google Chrome on the same system

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

* Reproducible in a minimal Electron application with only a single textarea element (no frameworks, no custom CSS, no layout complexity).
* Issue persists after testing multiple Electron versions (Electron 31 - Electron 35).
* Disabling CSS entirely (removing all styles) does not resolve the issue.
* Disabling GPU acceleration, changing backgroundThrottling, and other webPreferences flags do not affect the behavior.
* Same IME input method works correctly in:
    * Google Chrome (latest version on macOS)
    * Native macOS applications
* Suggests issue is specific to Electron/Chromium rendering path on macOS IME integration layer rather than application code or styling.
* Input composition (pre-edit text / pinyin) is correctly received, indicating IME is functional; only candidate window rendering/attachment is affected.
* Likely related to macOS IME candidate window attachment behavior in Electron’s Chromium-based web input pipeline under macOS 26.x (Tahoe).

nodes.title: [Bug]: SysDragImage top-level window leaked on Windows when drag completes in another application
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

Whatever ships with Discord 1.0.9236 (binary doesn't expose it cleanly in version metadata; see "Notes" below).

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Home, 10.0.26200 (build 26200)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — I haven't bisected. Behaviour observed in current shipping Discord client.

### Expected Behavior

When a drag operation initiated by an Electron application ends — regardless of whether the drop target is the same Electron window, a different window in the same process, a different application entirely, or `Esc`/cancel — the `SysDragImage` top-level window created by `IDragSourceHelper::InitializeFromBitmap` (or its `SetDragImage` cousin) should be destroyed.

### Actual Behavior

When the drag is consumed by a drop target in **another process** (in my repro: Chrome rendering claude.ai's file uploader), the `SysDragImage` window owned by the originating Electron process is **not destroyed**. It persists indefinitely as an orphan top-level window with the following Win32 styles:

- `WS_EX_TOPMOST` — sits over every other window
- `WS_EX_LAYERED` — alpha-composited
- `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` — passes mouse input through (so it can't be dismissed by clicking)
- `WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW` — invisible to Alt-Tab
- Class name: `SysDragImage`
- Window title: `Drag`
- Size: matches the drag-image bitmap (in my repro: 390×130 px at the position where the cursor was on drop)

Visually it appears as a stuck rectangle (white in my case, presumably whatever the failed-to-render drag-image bitmap was) floating on top of the desktop, surviving:

- The drop completing successfully in the receiving application.
- Closing the receiving application.
- Restarting `explorer.exe`.
- Pressing `Esc`, alt-tabbing, switching virtual desktops.

The only ways to clear it I have found:

1. Quit the originating Electron application (Discord), or
2. Surgically `PostMessage(hwnd, WM_CLOSE, 0, 0)` to the orphan HWND from a separate tool. The Electron process continues to run normally afterward — no functional regression observed.

### Testcase Gist URL

I do not have a minimal Electron testcase yet. The repro path requires whatever drag-source registration Discord performs. Happy to bisect / build a minimal Electron app that calls `webContents.startDrag` (or whatever Discord uses) if a maintainer thinks that would help isolate it from Discord-specific code.

### Additional Information

**Reproduction (Windows 11):**

1. Have Discord (1.0.9236) running with the main window visible. (The bug doesn't seem to require Discord to be focused.)
2. In Chrome, open https://claude.ai/ and start a chat (the file-upload drop target there triggers the bug; presumably any Chromium-rendered drop target in another process does).
3. From Windows File Explorer, drag any file into the claude.ai chat window. The drop succeeds — the file uploads normally.
4. Observe: a translucent rectangle, sized to the drag preview, remains painted on top of every window. Discord still works.

**Forensic evidence (PowerShell `EnumWindows` enumeration after the bug occurs):**

```
HWND=0x164140A  PID=8704 (Discord)
  Class:    SysDragImage
  Title:    Drag
  Size:     390x130 @ 947,587
  ExStyles: TopMost=True, Layered=True, Transparent=True, ToolWindow=True
```

PID 8704 was the Discord main process. Posting `WM_CLOSE` to that HWND alone clears the artefact and leaves Discord running:

```powershell
[W]::PostMessage(0x164140A, 0x0010, 0, 0)  # WM_CLOSE
# Window destroyed; Discord unaffected.
```

**Hypothesis on root cause:**

Chromium's drag-source code on Windows uses `IDragSourceHelper::InitializeFromBitmap` to register a drag image with the Windows shell. The shell creates the `SysDragImage` top-level window to render the bitmap and follows the cursor through the drag. Cleanup is supposed to occur when the drag completes (in `IDropSource::QueryContinueDrag` returning `DRAGDROP_S_DROP`/`DRAGDROP_S_CANCEL`, or via the shell's own teardown when the drag-drop session ends).

The leak appears to be specific to drops that occur in a **different OS-level drop target** than the source. When source and target are both inside the same Chromium/Electron app, cleanup happens. When the target is an external HWND owned by another process (Chrome.exe in this case, presumably any non-Electron drop target), the source's drag-end callback either doesn't fire or doesn't reach the cleanup path that destroys the `SysDragImage` HWND.

This is consistent with similar drag-source lifecycle bugs that have surfaced in adjacent contexts:

- Vencord/Vesktop#541 — Linux: Vesktop's input handling breaks until relaunch after a cross-app drag. Different OS surface, plausibly the same lifecycle bug.
- electron/electron#39839 — Drag-and-drop spawning a phantom Electron window plus a save dialog in 27.0.0-beta.1.
- swaywm/wlroots#2889 — Drag image freezes in Chromium/Electron on X11/Wayland.

I do not have a Chromium repro outside Discord — happy to build one if useful.

### Notes

- I am reporting this against `electron/electron` rather than Chromium upstream because (a) Electron is the actually-shipping surface where this manifests, (b) the Electron team triages to Chromium when appropriate, and (c) public Chromium bug filing has friction. Feel free to redirect to crbug.com if that's the cleaner home.
- Discord ships its Electron build without exposing the version through standard binary metadata (`Discord.exe` advertises `ProductName=Discord, Description=Discord` only). I can't tell you the exact Electron version without invasive inspection.
- The originating drag may have been a OneDrive-virtualised file (the source folder was OneDrive-synced), which involves the OneDrive shell extension hydrating the file via `dllhost.exe`. I cannot rule out that this is a contributing factor — i.e. the leak might only occur when the drag-source data object involves shell-extension hydration. Worth checking with a non-OneDrive source.

nodes.title: [Bug] webRequest.onBeforeRequest's redirectURL is ignored for WebSocket requests
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.5.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.3.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

None

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

In the Gist is a fiddle which sets a `webRequest.onBeforeRequest` handler to intercept the WebSocket connection which is made in `renderer.js`.

The Electron main process logs should show these logs:

```
Proxying WebSocket from wss://echo.websocket.org/ to local server
New WebSocket connection: ......
[client→server]Ping!
[server→client]Ping!
```

The first log line is from when we setup the interception.

The second is when the renderer connects through the WebSocket proxy.

The third and fourth are from the messages sent through the proxy.

Inside the Renderer you should see these messages on the screen to show what happened with the WebSocket connection:

```
[ws/open]
[ws/message] Request served by XXXXXXXX
[ws/message] Ping!
```

### Actual Behavior

The logs in the Electron main process are just:

```
Proxying WebSocket from wss://echo.websocket.org/ to local server
```

This indicates that the `webRequest.onBeforeRequest` handler is being called correctly, but as no other logs follow the WebSocket connection is not being correctly redirected to the proxy.

The logs inside the renderer are correct. Showing it is connecting to and communicating with the echo server.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/fede254f6a62f0c95abc18c990abc122

### Additional Information

It seems to me like the `ProxyingWebSocket::ContinueToHeadersReceived` method is not correctly handling `redirect_url_`: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/99117903fe94b9959f4c26a3b04d3e773749ae7d/shell/browser/net/proxying_websocket.cc#L95-L115

I beleive the code for standard requests is here: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/99117903fe94b9959f4c26a3b04d3e773749ae7d/shell/browser/net/proxying_url_loader_factory.cc#L509-L512

Related issue which was close due to lack of reproduction: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/31191

### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.0.0-beta.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Win10

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Resize area should start right at the edge of the content area

### Actual Behavior

Resize area starts within the content area

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Related: https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50706

> Corrects the placement of resize hit targets for frameless windows on Windows, which are supposed to be outside the window at the sides and bottom, not inset into the web content.

When I create a simple window
```
const mainWindow1 = new BrowserWindow({
		x: 0,
		y: 0,
		width: 1000,
		height: 600,
		show: true,
		frame: false,
	});
```
I can still see a few pixels of resize area being within the content area. The area does go outside of the window but starts within the content area.
Is this intended?
@mitchchn

Window should not change its size

window gets smaller by the resize handle after moving it
